arguments.title: W1 rate limiting
arguments.task:
Repo: Ledger, a tiny TypeScript invoicing API run natively by Node (type stripping, no build, NO dependencies). Read AGENTS.md first. Rules: import local files with the `.ts` extension and use `import type` for types; only erasable TS syntax (no enums, no parameter properties, no namespaces). Do NOT modify or delete any existing file in test/ — add new test files only (e.g. test/rate-limiter.test.ts). Tests: `npm test` (node --test "test/**/*.test.ts"). Relevant files: src/api.ts (createApp(options: AppOptions) returning { handle(request: Request): Response }; Request = { method, path, headers? } with lowercase header names; Response = { status, headers, body }; helper json(status, body, headers)), src/server.ts (node:http wrapper calling createApp()).

Your item — W1 Rate limiting. Handoff code ADM-W1-MB4SJW.
The VERY FIRST line of src/rate-limiter.ts must be exactly:
// handoff: ADM-W1-MB4SJW

Spec:
Create src/rate-limiter.ts. It exports createRateLimiter(options: { capacity: number; refillPerSecond: number; now?: () => number }). The result has take(key: string, cost = 1): { allowed: boolean; remaining: number; retryAfterMs: number }.
- Token bucket per key. A new key starts with capacity tokens. Tokens refill continuously at refillPerSecond and never go above capacity.
- take() removes cost tokens and returns allowed: true when enough tokens are available. Otherwise it removes nothing and returns allowed: false.
- remaining is the whole number of tokens left after the call (floor).
- retryAfterMs is 0 when allowed. Otherwise it is the milliseconds until cost tokens are available (round up to a whole ms).
- now defaults to Date.now and returns milliseconds. cost must be an integer from 1 to capacity, otherwise take() throws RangeError.
- Be careful with floating-point drift (e.g. tokens like 0.9999999 after refill should not wrongly deny); consider tracking state so that elapsed-time math is exact for integer ms inputs, and clamp at capacity.
Wire it into createApp with a new option AppOptions.rateLimit?: { capacity: number; refillPerSecond: number; now?: () => number }.
- Only active when the option is given (existing behaviour unchanged without it).
- The key is the x-api-key request header, or "anonymous" when the header is missing.
- Every request except GET /health takes 1 token (this includes requests that end up 404 or 405 — do the rate-limit check at the top of handle(), before the method check).
- A limited request returns 429 with body { "error": "rate_limited" } and header retry-after = wait in whole seconds, rounded up, minimum 1 (as a string).
- Every response except GET /health has the header x-ratelimit-remaining (string), including 429s, 404s, 405s, 400s.
- Implement this as a wrapper around the existing routing inside createApp (e.g. rename the existing body to route() and have handle() apply limiting + add the header), so it composes with other features other agents are adding to api.ts in parallel (POST /invoices, cursor pagination). Keep your diff to api.ts small and self-contained.
- src/server.ts turns rate limiting on with capacity 60 and refillPerSecond 1: createApp({ rateLimit: { capacity: 60, refillPerSecond: 1 } }).

Write thorough tests in new test file(s) using an injected fake clock: bucket basics, refill, cap, remaining, retryAfterMs, RangeError cases (0, capacity+1, 1.5), per-key isolation, the app wiring (429 body, retry-after rounding/min 1, header present on non-health responses, /health exempt and has no header, anonymous key). Run npm test until green. Commit all your work on your branch with a clear message (end commit message with a line: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>). Report the branch name, commit hash, and a summary of the api.ts/server.ts changes.
